title: Never Growing Careless
note: Not growing careless about guarding yourself or destroying your enemies, through delight in your looks, fortune or power. Kin are of use only where there is no such lapse.

couplets.plain: Worse than boundless rage is the carelessness that comes from the high spirits of great delight.
couplets.pm: For a ruler, the forgetfulness that comes from excessive delight is worse than rage beyond measure. Such delight comes from great wealth, great pleasure and great pride. Anger in measure is needed to crush enemies and punish the wicked. Excessive anger at least sometimes kills the enemy, but this kills only you, so it is worse.

links.quote: Worse than boundless rage is the carelessness
links.reason: Rates carelessness born of delight as worse than the worst rage.

couplets.plain: Carelessness kills glory, as daily want kills understanding.
couplets.pm: A man’s forgetfulness destroys his glory, as daily begging to fill his belly destroys understanding. If a wise man has to beg each day, the disgrace and sin bring him scorn and his standing goes. In the same way a man of glory who is forgetful fails to guard himself and ruins his affairs, and scorn destroys his standing.
couplets.sensitive: says daily poverty kills a person’s understanding; could shame someone in want

links.reason: Sets carelessness beside want: one kills glory as the other kills understanding.

couplets.plain: There is no glory for the careless. The learned of every kind in the world agree on that.
couplets.pm: Those who live forgetfully have no glory. Not only writers on statecraft but the learned of every kind in the world agree on this. It shows that the rule holds not only for rulers but for anyone striving at any of the four aims, righteousness and the rest, since they fail in them and so have no glory.

links.quote: There is no glory for the careless

couplets.plain: There is no fort for those who are afraid. Just so, there is no good for the careless.
couplets.pm: Those with fear in their minds get no use from forts of forest or hill, even standing inside them. In the same way those with forgetfulness in their minds get no use from wealth of every kind. Good here means what brings good. As the fort of the fearful falls, the wealth of the forgetful is lost.

links.quote: no fort for those who are afraid
there is no good for the careless
links.reason: Nothing good stays with one who has stopped taking care.

couplets.plain: One who fails to guard in advance will regret that mistake when the blow lands.
couplets.pm: One who forgets and doesn’t guard in advance against troubles he could have prevented will grieve over that mistake when they come, because it is then too late to guard. The troubles are what enemies do when they see a lapse.

links.quote: will regret that mistake when the blow lands

couplets.plain: If you can keep from slipping, with everyone, at all times, without fail, nothing else compares.
couplets.pm: If rulers manage a mind that doesn’t forget, with anyone, at any time and without a lapse, no other good equals it. With anyone, because it must hold for their own workers and kin. At any time, because it must hold when they are growing and when they are shrinking. Without a lapse, because it must hold in all their affairs.

links.quote: with everyone, at all times, without fail

couplets.plain: Nothing is too hard to do, if you take care and use the tool of unbroken attention.
couplets.pm: No task is so hard that it can’t be done, if you think it through with a mind that doesn’t forget. The mind is called a tool because it is the inner organ. For those with unbroken thought and unfailing planning, everything is easily done.

couplets.plain: Hold to what is praised and do it. Those who scorn it and don’t do it have nothing, in all seven births.
couplets.pm: Hold firm to the acts that writers on statecraft exalt as proper to rulers. Those who forget them have no good in any of seven births. The acts are the three powers, four means, five tasks and six courses. Those who stray from the duty of their caste have only the pains of hell, which is why he says seven births.

links.quote: have nothing, in all seven births
links.reason: Neglect of what is praised leaves a person with nothing in all seven births.

links.remove: The Tamil names no ruler. He supplies one, and the old English follows him.

couplets.plain: When your delight makes you feel strong, remember those who were ruined by neglect.
couplets.pm: When rulers grow strong in their delight, let them think of those who were ruined in the past by the lapse it brings. Thinking of them, they see that they would be ruined the same way, and so they don’t grow strong in it. Neglect and ruin appear together.

links.quote: those who were ruined by neglect
When your delight makes you feel strong

couplets.plain: Getting what you have set your mind on is easy, if you can keep your mind on it.
couplets.pm: It is easy for a ruler to get what he has thought of getting, just as he thought it, if he can go on thinking of that alone. It hints that people can’t manage this. Keeping it in mind means striving at it without forgetting.

links.quote: if you can keep your mind on it

ideaLinks.reason: Carelessness is said to kill glory.
Daily want is said to kill understanding.

ideaLinks.quote: There is no glory for the careless
ideaLinks.reason: Glory is denied to the careless.
